subject: Food Science
title: Critical Control Points
description: A short lesson to help you apply Critical Control Points.

hook.text: In a chicken processing plant, the cooking step is a critical control point. Get it wrong and E. coli reaches consumers.

buildup.text: A CCP is any step where a hazard can be prevented, eliminated, or reduced to safe levels—and where failure means danger.

discovery.text: Each CCP has critical limits: cooking temperature, metal detector sensitivity, pH level—measurable values that define safety.

twist.text: Not every step is a CCP. Washing lettuce reduces bacteria but doesn't eliminate them—so it's a control point, not a CCP.

climax.text: Continuous monitoring at CCPs means taking measurements in real time—digital thermometers, inline sensors, automatic rejection.

punchline.text: A CCP is where safety is won or lost. Monitor it, control it, document it.

quiz.question: What defines a Critical Control Point?
options: A step where hazards can be prevented or eliminated and failure means danger
